bib.title: Skeleton-of-Thought: Prompting LLMs for Efficient Parallel Generation

read.skipped: Reference list and long figure number dumps skimmed; I.1.2-I.1.4 and I.2/I.4.5 worked answer examples and WizardLM-specific figures only skimmed.

question: Can an off-the-shelf LLM cut end-to-end generation latency by first writing a short answer skeleton and then expanding the points in parallel?
hypothesis: Many long answers have independently expandable points, so decoding them in parallel (batched decoding or parallel API calls) gives about B times faster decoding without hurting, and sometimes improving, quality.
contributions: Skeleton-of-Thought (SoT), a prompting method for parallel decoding of off-the-shelf LLMs
Evaluation on 12 LLMs of speed-up and answer quality
SoT-R, a router (GPT-4 prompting or trained RoBERTa) that triggers SoT only for suitable questions

method.summary: A two-stage prompting pipeline: a skeleton prompt yields 3-10 short points, then one point-expanding request per point is run in parallel (batched decoding locally, parallel API calls for hosted models) and concatenated. SoT-R adds a router deciding SoT or normal decoding. Nothing in the LLMs is trained; only the RoBERTa router is fine-tuned.
method.task: Latency reduction for open-ended chat answers; quality judged pairwise by an LLM judge

datasets.name: LIMA training set
datasets.size: 1,030 Q&As, annotated for SoT suitability (371 suitable)
datasets.preprocessing: Labelled 1 if GPT-4's answer has a list of parallel-expandable points each with enough detail; two authors annotated independently and reconciled

models.name: Vicuna-7B V1.3, V1.1; Vicuna-13B V1.3; Vicuna-33B V1.3

inference.decoding: Normal sequential decoding vs SoT: skeleton request, then B point-expanding requests as a left-padded batch (local) or parallel API calls
inference.samples: Latency profiling: decode each setting 3 times (geometric mean); prefill 7 runs, first 2 warmup, geometric mean of last 5. Actual latency test: 5 runs per model. Quality: one answer per question per model, judged with both orderings.
inference.prompting: Skeleton prompt (3-5 word points, 3-10 points); 2-shot demos for all models except GPT-4; point-expanding prompt 'very shortly in 1~2 sentence' (dropped for Claude and GPT-4); partial answer '1.' / '{point index}. {point skeleton}' supplied to continue; no system message except LLaMA2

parameters.router_training: AdamW, weight decay 0.01, lr 5e-5 (warm-up first 1% then linear decay), 2 epochs, batch 32, seq 512, Tversky loss alpha 0.7 beta 0.3, label smoothing 0.2, 2 min on A100

other.software: CUDA 11.7, Hugging Face transformers 4.28.1, PyTorch 2.0.1, FastChat conversation templates
other.latency_profile: Tables for LLaMA 7B/13B/33B: prefill lengths 1..691 step 10, batch 1-16; decode context 1..1024, batch 1-16; T = prefill + sum of decode steps (Eq 1)
other.API_latency: skeleton call latency plus slowest point-expanding call, via time.time()

metrics.name: Speed-up
metrics.definition: Latency of normal generation divided by latency of SoT (or SoT-R) generation

metrics.name: Win/tie/lose rate
metrics.definition: Per-question GPT-4 pairwise judgement, run twice with both answer orders; scores +1/0/-1 summed; positive=win, zero=tie, negative=lose

baselines: Normal sequential generation with the same model
eval.protocol: FastChat (general metric; special prompts for math and coding) and LLMZoo (general plus coherence, diversity, immersion, integrity, relevance; math and coding excluded) with GPT-4 judge; ChatGPT-3.5 judge in App I.4. No human evaluation, no significance tests.

prompts.text: You're an organizer responsible for only giving the skeleton (not the full content) for answering the question. Provide the skeleton in a list of points (numbered 1., 2., 3., etc.) to answer the question. Instead of writing a full sentence, each skeleton point should be very short with only 3∼5 words. Generally, the skeleton should have 3∼10 points. Now, please provide the skeleton for the following question. {question} Skeleton: [Assistant:] 1.

You're responsible for continuing the writing of one and only one point in the overall answer to the following question. {question} The skeleton of the answer is {skeleton} Continue and only continue the writing of point {point index}. Write it **very shortly** in 1∼2 sentence and do not continue with other points! [Assistant:] {point index}. {point skeleton}

Question: {question} How would you like to answer the question? A. Organize the answer as a list of points or perspectives (in the format of 1., 2., 3., etc.), and the points or perspectives can be answered independently without referring to the contents of the previous points. B. Organize the answer as a list of points or perspectives (in the format of 1., 2., 3., etc.), and the contents of later points or perspectives cannot be answered independently without referring to the contents of the previous ones. C. Do not organize the answer as a list of points or perspectives. Just say A, B, or C. Do not explain. Do not provide an answer to the question.

results.claim: SoT gives more than 2x end-to-end speed-up on 8 of 12 models, up to 2.39x.
results.setup: Vicuna-80 (80 questions), 12 models, latency estimated from A100 profiling tables (open-source) or measured API latency
results.quote: We can see that SoT obtains a >2× speed-up (up to 2.39×) on 8 out of 12 models.

results.claim: StableVicuna-13B gets almost no speed-up because it ignores the 'very shortly' instruction.
results.setup: Vicuna-80 (80 questions), 12 models, latency estimated from A100 profiling tables (open-source) or measured API latency
results.quote: Consequently, SoT cannot accelerate StableVicuna-13B well.

results.claim: On the five categories where SoT keeps quality, speed-up is 1.89x to 2.33x.
results.setup: Vicuna-80 (80 questions), 12 models, latency estimated from A100 profiling tables (open-source) or measured API latency, averaged over models
results.quote: SoT can speed up the overall answer generation process by 1.89× to 2.33× in the meantime.

results.claim: Math has the lowest speed-up by category.

results.setup: Vicuna-80, 9 open-source models, 5 runs each, single A100, real batch testing
results.quote: SoT achieves no speed-up on StableVicuna-13B.

results.claim: Intro example: Claude 22s to 12s and Vicuna-33B 43s to 16s on one question.

results.claim: Quality: SoT is not worse than normal in about 60% of cases; strictly better in 45.8% (LLMZoo) vs 29.5% (FastChat).
results.setup: Vicuna-80, all 12 models, GPT-4 judge, both answer orderings
results.quote: We notice a discrepancy between the two metrics on when SoT is strictly better than the baseline (45.8% v.s. 29.5%).

results.claim: SoT improves diversity and relevance, hurts immersion and coherence.
results.setup: Vicuna-80 excluding math and coding, LLMZoo metrics, GPT-4 judge
results.quote: On average, we can see that SoT improves the diversity and relevance while hurting the immersion and coherence.

results.quote: SoT performs relatively well on generic, common-sense, knowledge, roleplay, and counterfactual, and relatively poorly on writing, fermi, math, and coding.

limits: Quality evaluation relies on GPT-4 judges with possible bias, a small prompt set (80 and 218 questions), no human evaluation (authors say SoT answers are easy to recognise).
Unsuited to step-by-step reasoning (math, coding) and short answers; SoT ignores dependencies between points.
Speed-up depends on prompt, model, question, so less predictable than model- or system-level methods; StableVicuna-13B gets no speed-up.
Helps latency only when concurrent queries are unsaturated; under load, prefill overhead (about 30x to 89x prefill tokens) hurts throughput and API cost.
Open-source speed-ups are mostly estimated from A100 profiling tables for LLaMA architectures; real batch test covers 9 open-source models only.
Decoding temperature, max tokens and seeds are not stated.
